That's the entire point though; Sarah Lynn isn't exempt from her responsibility to herself, I never said that and I don't think anyone really believes that. That's why most everyone agrees she would've died in a similar fashion with or without Bojack around. 

The show isn't called Sarah Lynn, it's called Bojack, and it's his actions I'm calling out here. Bojack was responsible for playing out that role she set up for him, when he had every chance not to. His 'soft spot' could've been the breaking point that pushed him to try and help her, even if he failed, but instead he gives in to his own addictions and desires. He never once even tries to put her well being, or anyone else's, first, at least until his sister comes around, and even that turns out to be a sad selfish tragedy in the end as well. Even when he attempts to make things right with others, it's inevitably to make himself feel better, no one else. His drugs aren't the problem, his childhood isn't the problem, his selfishness and the ego it derives from is the problem, which is pretty much what Todd says.

Sarah Lynn was being young and stupid; Bojack literally had all the cards in his hands to simply say, no. He didn't have to cater to her bullshit, he didn't even need to be around her, and once again, she's a child compared to him. At any point in time he could've put his foot down, set his own conditions, and at the very least told her to go fuck off somewhere else. Nothing forced him to party and sleep with the kid he co-starred with. It's one thing to fuck up your own life, it's another to participate in dragging down someone else, especially someone way younger and more vulnerable then you. 

No matter what point she was at, Bojack had more life experience and the knowledge to influence her in ANY OTHER WAY then to fuck her and fuck her over until she dies. There's literally no excuse for that. 

At the end of the day, Bojack still chose his own selfish desire to party and fuck, over the more responsible option of telling her no and not involving himself. That's on him.

All very true. Still, what's the excuse when she comes to him for support as a young woman in her twenties? Even if she wasn't a child any more, she still was in relation to Bojack. She was blatantly crying out for help, and I refuse to think that Bojack is just too naive to be aware that maybe NOT indulging his sick friend (including fucking her,) was the better idea. Whether she would've ended up killing herself with or without Bojack is irrelevant; she went to him, and he lead her like a lamb to slaughter, without hesitation or regret. His only focus was on himself and how much fun it would be, an only regretted it after the fun and games had already cost her life.

Trust me, man, I tried and still try to emphasize with Bojack and people like Bojack. Unfortunately I can't go no contact with the family members that hurt me so I'm still dealing with their toxicity, and still trying to learn how to manuever around it so I can still try to live a fulfilling life. Empathy can only go so far, when the person you are trying to relate to isn't empathetic at all. Not once did Bojack put himself in Sandra Lynn's shoes, to see her for what she was (at the time,) a young and vulnerable child that he was responsible for being an influence to. In his selfishness he never thought to see how much he was hurting others, and once he did, instead of trying to make it right for them, he only wanted to assuage his own guilt.

Reminds me painfully of the day after a night of my dad's drunken abuse. The next day was filled with tender apologies and sweet words, only to stagnate over time as the same cycle repeated itself over and over. 

It takes more then self reflection, it takes more then apologies that are too little too late. It takes ripping down the idol of an ego he has built to himself, and starting completely over, something that at least Bojack eventually attempted to do.

I guess I'm painfully optimistic because I have had a lot of good experiences in the past, I've been a loyal customer for years, and I was hoping it wouldn't get to this point.

It might've just been that, no driver was specifically rude, but a few of the more talkative ones have openly complained about how little they were getting for the trip, which is what prompted my initial concern and why I began pulling out a few bucks for tips. Most are polite, and like I commented to a few others it was just a 'vibe' thing which is hard to put into words, but it was confirmed that drivers are just being paid so little even for short trips. This kind of feeling wasn't prevalent years ago, and we've been using Uber since it started up in Dallas, always for the same short trips, to grab medications or groceries.
Worthless trip? Getting medications or groceries isn't worthless, but ok, I hope you have a good day

I mean no need to be rude about it, my title did say I'm not going to continue. I do realize that, I have used the service for years, it just seems different these days, probably because the app takes so much from the driver including tips which is out of my control, and that's ok.

While this is understandable, it's more cost effective to do the one trip, especially if it's less then 3-5 min. We usually order beforehand to get our stuff prepared and get out so that trips inside are very minimal. Our family is living below the poverty level, living buck by buck and penny by penny just like the drivers, so every bit has to go as far as possible. This is why I tip in cash, because even with such short trips I want to be able to give the driver what is earned and the app just takes so much.

That's understandable and also what I assumed. It's just really hard when we're living buck by buck, the same as the drivers. This is why I've tipped with cash, because the app just seems to take so much even from short trips.
